# Methods

This chapter describes the experimental design of the thesis. Every tabular foundation model in the experiments is evaluated frozen. The pretrained weights are used exactly as published, and no fine-tuning or any other gradient update is applied [@thomas2024localpfn_retrieval_finetuning]. The only element that varies is test-time context construction, meaning which labelled training rows fill the context window and at what class ratio. As @sec-bg-pfn established, the context is the only task-specific information the model conditions on, so the context is the natural point of intervention.

The research questions of @sec-intro-rqs decompose into pairwise contrasts between the four context-construction conditions C1 to C4. The step from C1 to C2 isolates the effect of the in-context fraud ratio (RQ2). The step from C1 to C3 varies the relevance of the context (RQ3). The step from C3 to C4 adds ratio control on top of retrieval, and the comparison of C4 against C2 answers whether retrieval adds anything beyond plain rebalancing (RQ4). The comparison between best performing experimental conditions and GBDTs will answer the feasibility of these models working with extremely imbalanced datasetd (RQ1). This decomposition is the spine of the design. The rest of the chapter defines the conditions and the machinery that runs them.

## Experimental conditions {#sec-methods-conditions}

Condition 1 (random) fills the context with a uniform random subsample of the training set, drawn up to the model's context limit. The fraud ratio of the context thus follows the natural prevalence of the data. This is the standard practice whose cost @sec-context-waste quantified, and it serves as the baseline for every other condition.

Condition 2 (stratified) balances the context toward a 50/50 class split. All available fraud rows enter the context, capped at half of the window, and the remaining slots are filled with randomly drawn legitimate rows. On datasets whose training split holds fewer fraud rows than half the window, the realised ratio therefore stays below 50/50. <!-- TODO: adding a inline r that fetches the real fraud ratios. And list them then here. --> Both classes are still drawn at random, so the contrast between C2 and C1 gives the effect of rebalancing the classes while relevance is held fixed.

Condition 3 (kNN control) fills the context by kNN retrieval around clusters of the scored test transactions, without touching the class ratio. <!-- TODO: crossref the RAP pipeline section once it exists --> The realised fraud share is therefore not fixed but fluctuates with the local neighbourhood of each cluster. <!-- TODO: adding a inline r that fetches the real fraud ratios from different runs. And list them then here. --> The contrast between C3 and C1 consequently varies relevance without holding the ratio fixed. Relevance is isolated cleanly only by the ratio-matched ablation described later in this chapter. <!-- TODO: crossref the relevance-ablation section once it exists --> The unmatched form is kept deliberately, because it asks a question of its own. Does a TFM need to see fraudulent transactions from far regions of the feature space, or is the relevant region alone enough?

Condition C4 is the full RAP configuration. Retrieval becomes stratified, with a separate kNN retriever per class, so that relevant observations are drawn from both classes. On top of this, the fraud ratio of the context is enforced and swept over 5 %, 10 %, 20 %, 30 % and 50 %. <!-- TODO: Add another 'natural' level RAP to check with c3  relevance-ablation --> When the unique fraud rows near a cluster run out before the quota is filled, fraud rows are duplicated by sampling with replacement. This oversampling is part of the method rather than a fallback. <!-- TODO: We need similar duplication sweep for c2 as well.--> The step from C3 to C4 is thus not just a single-factor change, it both enforces the ratio and swaps mixed retrieval for stratified retrieval. The sweep within C4 in turn isolates ratio tuning on a fixed retrieval mechanism.

The GBDT baselines run under C1 only and are trained on the full training set. The context limit is an inherent property of TFMs, so the most informative comparison for RQ1 is the full-data GBDT against the context-limited TFM. The context budget is 10,000 rows for TabPFN v2, the hard limit of its checkpoint. The remaining models run at a budget of roughly 50,000 rows. This figure is a design choice made for cross-model comparability, not the maximum of every checkpoint. <!-- TODO: future abblation to test all models at their best condition with the biggest context windows possible -->
